purpose.summary: Release native chain and mempool locks after at most 64 startup metadata rows, rejecting source drift before publishing the owned graph.
scope: Direct child of signed public main dd349dca integrated by PR62; five technical postimages plus finite source policy, documentation and CI.
Preallocate the existing bounded metadata buffer, reacquire a hash cursor for each batch and retain only values across lock boundaries.
Bind healthy profile, chain and pool generations, tip, map size and bucket count before every batch and after the last batch.
Retain all 57 inherited archival native case bodies, all existing service clients and the exact atomic final storage fence.
Add five fresh-process cases with 54 assertions under the existing 60-second per-process deadline.
exclusions: No mainnet admission, service budget or default change; no production startup retry policy.
No upstream indexer, ALP parser/builder, plugin engine, dependency, consensus, network identity, RPC or wallet change.
No incoming report, private history, operator data, server access, deployment, cutover, release, desktop integration or proof promotion.

commands: Build the exact public compiled-out profile with unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The standalone node builds without Chronik linkage and retains all inherited controls.

commands: Build the exact public compiled-in-disabled profile with existing locked Rust inputs and unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The standalone node builds with runtime Chronik disabled by default and retains all inherited controls.

commands: Build the exact public regtest-plugins profile with existing locked Rust inputs and unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The daemon and native fixture build; inherited profiles retain their existing boundaries.

scenarios.command: Run the five-case startup-metadata-batches group, then the unchanged owned-startup group and all inherited profile-bound groups in fresh processes.
expected_results: Five cases and 54 assertions pass; copied batch sizes never exceed 64, another thread acquires both locks after each batch, drift/cancellation never publish a graph.
The retained owned-startup group remains four cases and 607 assertions; all inherited clients and fixed deadlines are preserved.
failure_conditions: Wrong case/assertion count, batch exceeding 64, lock handoff blocked, stale source/cursor accepted, partial owner published, source/build drift, timeout, skip, nonzero exit or cleanup failure.

limitations: The complete metadata buffer and owned graph remain O(indexes); this slice bounds copy work per lock acquisition, not peak RSS or lock latency.
Final storage identity validation remains a complete atomic pass; batching it requires a storage mutation generation or equivalent native contract.
Runtime remains unpruned local regtest, maximum height 2000, indexes 4096 and mempool entries 4096, with all inherited payload and reorganization budgets.
A capture crossing chain/pool/map drift fails before publication and performs no automatic retry; continuous-ingress startup liveness is not established.
The next-hash cursor relies on native index lifetime retained until joined teardown; live index erase/replacement is not supported.
System build dependencies remain unlocked; no reproducible-build, full-history, operator-plugin or mainnet-readiness claim.
counterevidence: Historical startup and aggregate stop/reopen timeouts and upstream dependency alerts remain open.
No server, operator datadir, mainnet history or production replacement is exercised.
